html:
In 1573 Muhammad Thakurufaanu and his brothers drove the Portuguese garrison out of Male, ending about fifteen years of Portuguese rule over the Maldives. He then ruled as sultan until his death in 1585.

The Portuguese, based at Goa, had taken Male in 1558 and wanted the islands' trade in cowries and coir. Thakurufaanu, from the northern island of Utheemu, raised a band of fighters and, tradition says, raided the occupiers from a boat among the atolls for years before a surprise attack took the capital.

His family founded a new line of sultans. The day of the victory is kept each year as National Day. His story made the defence of Islam and of Muslim self-rule the core of Maldivian identity, seen again in the islands' independence in 1965.
